text:
Alice Morgan: FYI escalated ticket from @acme-banking — big p99 spike after yesterday's runtime release. They reported p99 went from ~620ms -> ~3.1s on chat and embeddings routes. They say it started immediately after they flipped auto-quantize for their model.

Diego Ramos: Customer says they toggled quant_profile=auto in the console; we got a support bundle (logs + traces). Attaching trace: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/abc123 (customer-visible).

deploy-bot: deploy/runtime-v2026-03-10 finished in 74s — feature: enable_auto_quantization=true

Ben Patel: Looking — can you paste a minimal repro request and the model id? Are requests large or short? p95 also bad or just tail?

Alice Morgan: Minimal curl we used to repro in-house:
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"gptx-3b-quant-v2","input":"short prompt","config":{"quant_profile":"int8","calibration":true}}'
```
Small payloads, not long contexts. p95 increased from 200ms -> ~450ms but p99 is the big jump to 3s.

Ben Patel: Hmm. That pattern smells like synchronous calibration/fallbacks. If runtime does "calibrate_on_first_request" and calibration fails we currently fallback to fp16 but that fallback path triggers weight layout conversions and may cause a blocking path (memory moves, kernel JIT), which can produce 2-3s spikes. Do we have any logs from the model host showing quant_calibration failures?

Alice Morgan: From the support bundle (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-10 14:09:22] model=gptx-3b-quant-v2 level=warn msg="calibration: unstable dynamic range"
[2026-03-10 14:09:22] model=gptx-3b-quant-v2 level=info msg="falling back to fp16" fallback_time_ms=2040
[2026-03-10 14:09:22] model=gptx-3b-quant-v2 level=info msg="runtime: triggered kernel re-layout, blocking"
```

Carla Nguyen: From ML side: INT8 calibration for this architecture is sensitive to initial activation stats; fp8 toggles introduced in the last model packaging created a slightly different weight layout and shifted the activation distributions. We shipped a more aggressive default: calibrate_on_first_request=true to speed up deployment, but that means the first requests can block while running calibration. If calibration fails once, we fall back to fp16 and still pay the cost of conversion.

Ben Patel: Immediate mitigations I propose (low-risk, quick):
1) disable live calibration for the affected model(s) by setting quantization.auto_calibrate=false in runtime overrides.
2) pin a routing override to the fp16 variant for customer-acme-banking until we have a stable int8 profile.
3) add an alert: quant.calibration_sync_count > 0 AND p99 > baseline -> P1 page.

Config snippet to apply as a route override:
```yaml
route:
  model: gptx-3b-quant-v2
  overrides:
    quantization:
      mode: int8
      auto_calibrate: false
      fallback: fp16
```

Repro steps I used locally (matches support curl above):
1) run the curl above against a canary host (EXAMPLE: https://canary.api.redwood.ai)
2) tail model host logs: sudo journalctl -u redwood-model-serve -f | grep quant
3) watch for "calibration" warnings + "falling back to fp16" lines and corresponding spike in request latency.

Ben Patel: Example log that lines up with the customer's spike: 
```
[14:09:22] quant: calibration_failed reason="unstable dynamic range"
[14:09:22] quant: fallback_initiated to=fp16 duration_ms=2040
[14:09:22] runtime: kernel_relayout blocking=true duration_ms=1980
```

Diego Ramos: I applied the route override to pin to fp16 for the customer's deployment at 14:12 UTC and flipped auto_calibrate=false. Notified customer into the ticket.

Alice Morgan: Customer just replied — p99 back to ~670ms, p95 ~430ms, they confirm much better UX. :thumbsup:

Carla Nguyen: Root cause summary: the new auto-calibration-on-first-request combined with recent fp8/int8 packaging changes produced unstable calibrations for a subset of inputs. The runtime's synchronous calibration + fallback path causes long-tail latency.

Ben Patel: Next actions (we've created INFRA-2437):
- Revert default for auto_calibrate to false in runtime release (hotfix).
- Implement async offline calibration pipeline & pre-warm model by shipping quantized weights where possible (ML).
- Add metrics: quant.calibration_sync_count, quant.fallback_count and correlate with p99; create alerting rule.
- Update runbook for support: quick mitigation steps (pin to fp16, set auto_calibrate=false, route to dedicated instance).

Carla Nguyen: Longer-term: require N successful offline calibrations before enabling int8 auto-rollout; add calibration stability test in CI.

Diego Ramos: I'll follow up with the customer and close the ticket after 24h of stable metrics. Thanks team.

Ben Patel: I'll ship the hotfix to revert the default and file a follow-up PR for async calibration. Tracking INFRA-2437 and ENG-ML-621.

Alice Morgan: Leaving this thread open until INFRA-2437 is triaged. Good triage — nice quick rollback and communication. :rocket:
